title: Best Books for SSC CGL 2026: Suggested Titles by Section
description: Commonly used SSC CGL books for Quant, Reasoning, English, GA and Computer, with what each suits and how to avoid buying too many. Suggestions only.
intro: There is no single best book for SSC CGL; the syllabus is fixed and several standard titles cover it. This guide lists **commonly used books by section**, who each one suits, and a simple rule for not over-buying. These are suggestions based on common use among aspirants, not rankings or endorsements, and we do not use affiliate links.

sections.title: How to choose and how many to buy
sections.body:
- **One main source per subject, plus previous-year questions (PYQs) and mocks.** More books rarely means more marks; unfinished books do not help.
- **Match the book to your level.** A foundation-level book for weak basics, an advanced one only after you can finish the standard set in time.
- **Pick the latest edition you can find** so that questions reflect the current pattern, and check that the answers are explained, not only listed.
- **Practice beats reading.** For Quant, Reasoning and English, the book is a question bank. For GA, it is a revision source.
- **Free options exist.** NCERT textbooks are free from the official NCERT website, and this site offers [topic notes with practice](/quant/percentage/), a [formula sheet](/formula-sheet/), [vocabulary](/vocab/), [daily quiz](/daily-quiz/) and [mocks](/exams/ssc-cgl/mocks/).

Titles below are mentioned as widely used; check the contents and a sample chapter before you buy, and rely on your own judgement of what suits your learning style.

sections.title: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.body:
| Book | Suits | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NCERT Mathematics, classes 6 to 10 | Weak basics, long gaps since school | Free; rebuilds fractions, percentages, algebra, geometry and mensuration fundamentals |
| R.S. Aggarwal, *Quantitative Aptitude for Competitive Examinations* | First pass through arithmetic and DI | Large question bank with explanations; many candidates use it as the base |
| Rajesh Verma, *Fast Track Objective Arithmetic* | Candidates who want more shortcuts and a larger set of arithmetic practice | Arithmetic-focused; pair with a geometry source |
| Rakesh Yadav, *Elementary and Advanced Mathematics* / *Advanced Maths* | After arithmetic is comfortable; targeted at Geometry, Algebra, Trigonometry and Mensuration | Useful for Tier 2 level questions, which are harder than Tier 1 |
| Chapter-wise solved paper books for SSC CGL (for example from Kiran Prakashan) | Everyone, from the build phase | See real question styles; always time yourself |

Suggested route: NCERT only if needed, then one arithmetic book, then one advanced-maths source, then PYQs. Topic-wise notes and shortcuts are also on this site, for example [Geometry](/quant/geometry/), [Data Interpretation](/quant/data-interpretation/) and [Trigonometry](/quant/trigonometry/).

sections.title: Reasoning
sections.body:
| Book | Suits | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| R.S. Aggarwal, *A Modern Approach to Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning* | Most candidates as a single base book | Covers both verbal and figure-based types with solved examples |
| M.K. Pandey, *Analytical Reasoning* | Candidates who want more depth on puzzles and logical sets | Heavier than needed for Tier 1; useful for Tier 2 puzzle practice |
| Chapter-wise PYQ compilations | Everyone | Reasoning on the exam is pattern-based; seeing the repeated patterns saves time |

Reasoning is a practice subject. One good book and daily timed sets of 20 to 30 questions generally work better than three books read once. Pair it with the high-frequency types on this site: [Series](/reasoning/series/), [Analogy](/reasoning/analogy/), [Coding-Decoding](/reasoning/coding-decoding/) and [Seating Arrangement](/reasoning/seating-arrangement/).

sections.title: English
sections.body:
| Book | Suits | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| P.C. Wren and H. Martin, *High School English Grammar and Composition* | Weak grammar basics | Reference for rules; do not read it cover to cover |
| S.P. Bakshi, *Objective General English* | Grammar and vocabulary practice in the objective format | Topic-wise question sets |
| Neetu Singh, *Plinth to Paramount* | Candidates who want a structured grammar and vocabulary path | Often used for SSC-style English |
| Norman Lewis, *Word Power Made Easy* | Vocabulary building over several weeks | Root-based approach; supplement with daily word lists |
| Daily editorial or newspaper reading | Everyone | Builds speed for [Reading Comprehension](/english/reading-comprehension/) and [Cloze Test](/english/cloze-test/) |

Spend about half your English time on vocabulary and reading, and half on grammar practice. Tier 2 English has 45 questions (135 marks), so it is worth building the habit early.

sections.title: General Awareness and Computer Knowledge
sections.body:
| Source | Suits | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| *Lucent's General Knowledge* | Static GK and general science revision | Concise, fact-oriented; verify dynamic facts with a recent source |
| NCERT Science, classes 6 to 10 | Biology, Physics and Chemistry | Free; matches the school-level questions asked |
| NCERT History and Geography, classes 6 to 12 (selected chapters) | History, geography | Use chapter summaries, not every page |
| Spectrum, *A Brief History of Modern India* (Rajiv Ahir) | Modern history | A compact reference; selective reading is enough |
| M. Laxmikanth, *Indian Polity* | Polity | Written for civil-service exams; read selected chapters only |
| Monthly current-affairs compilations or news | Current affairs (the single largest GA block) | Use the last 6 to 8 months before the exam; also see [current affairs](/current-affairs/) |
| A concise computer awareness guide | Computer Knowledge (Tier 2, qualifying) | Basics only: fundamentals, MS Office, internet, networking and security; see [Computer Fundamentals](/computer/computer-fundamentals/) and [Excel](/computer/ms-excel/) |

For GA, books are for revision and facts change; follow current affairs from a dated, reliable source. Keep the notes short and revise them on a cycle (day 1, 7, 21).

sections.title: Previous-year papers and mock tests
sections.body:
- **PYQs.** Solve at least the last 3 to 4 years of Tier 1 and Tier 2 papers by topic, first untimed, then timed. Memory-based papers circulated by coaching sites can differ from the real exam, so use them for patterns, not as exact questions.
- **Mocks.** Choose one or two series and take them regularly with full analysis. Our own [mocks](/exams/ssc-cgl/mocks/) follow the Tier 1 format.
- **Pattern check.** Compare what you practise with the [exam pattern](/exams/ssc-cgl/exam-pattern/) and [syllabus](/exams/ssc-cgl/syllabus/) pages, and always confirm the latest pattern on ssc.gov.in.

A reasonable shopping list for most candidates is four to six items: one Quant arithmetic book, one advanced-maths source, one reasoning book, one English grammar and vocabulary source, one GA source, and a PYQ book.

sections.title: What to avoid
sections.body:
- Do not buy books because a friend completed them; completion depends on how the book was used.
- Do not start a second book on a topic before finishing the first.
- Do not use outdated GA books for current affairs.
- Do not read without solving; for Quant and Reasoning, solving timed sets is the real work.

Reviews and rankings of books are subjective, and results depend far more on practice and analysis than on the title. Treat this list as a starting point and adjust to your own level.

faqs.q: Which is the best book for SSC CGL Quant?
faqs.a: There is no single best. Many candidates use R.S. Aggarwal or Rajesh Verma for arithmetic and Rakesh Yadav for advanced maths, along with chapter-wise solved papers. Choose according to your level and finish one source before starting another.

faqs.q: Do I need a different book for Tier 2?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. Tier 2 uses the same syllabus with harder questions, so an advanced-maths source and more English practice are the usual additions, along with Tier 2 pattern mocks.

faqs.q: Are NCERT books enough for GA?
faqs.a: NCERT Science, History and Geography cover the school-level core, but you also need current affairs and a static GK source. Add polity and economy revision from a concise book.

faqs.q: Can I prepare without buying books?
faqs.a: Yes, to a large extent. NCERT textbooks are free, and this site has topic notes, formula sheet, vocabulary, daily quiz and mocks. A solved-papers book and one question bank per section still help.

faqs.q: How many books are too many?
faqs.a: More than one main source per subject is usually too many. Finish one book or one question bank before starting another, and keep time for PYQs and mocks.
